name: Countdown Display
author: ChuckBuilds
description: Create and manage customizable countdowns with images. Perfect for birthdays, holidays, events, and special occasions.

versions.notes: Scale the image to the area it is actually given. The image area defaulted to a third of the display width for every layout preset, including 'image-only' -- which draws no text, so the whole panel is available. A 256x64 banner on a 128x32 board came out 42x10 instead of 128x32, and 'image-only' rendered identically to 'image-left'. The image-left and image-right presets are unchanged: they still reserve a third of the width for the image and give the rest to the text, and an explicit image_width/image_height from the advanced settings still wins over both. Also stopped dropping extreme aspect ratios: fitting a very wide or very tall source rounded its short side down to zero, which Image.resize rejects, so the image vanished with only a log line -- it is now clamped to one pixel.

Make the colour settings work. Every draw_text call passed a font but no color, so the core drew all text white: font_color, name_font_color (default grey), each countdown's style.font_color / style.name_font_color, and the yellow highlight for the last 24 hours did nothing. The colours were only handed to the font manager's registration, which never draws with them. With the defaults the name line now renders in its documented grey rather than white; goldens refreshed. Countdowns are now also computed against wall-clock time in the LEDMatrix timezone setting instead of the Pi's system zone, falling back to system time when none is set.

Make every font in the picker actually work. Only two of the five offered families rendered: tiny and picopixel have no font file anywhere, and every bitmap family fell back silently because a .bdf exists at exactly one pixel size and the loader asked for font_size. Bitmap faces are now loaded at the size the file's PIXEL_SIZE header declares, and bitmap families use the plugin's own loader even when the core's catalog claims them -- the core resolver degrades to the default face without signalling it, which is why five_by_seven silently did nothing. tom_thumb is wired up (the file was always shipped, just unmapped), and the enum now lists the four families that verifiably render distinctly: press_start, four_by_six, five_by_seven, tom_thumb. Also rewrites the README around real rendered screenshots and documents all 40 settings, including the countdown-value ladder, which the old README got wrong: there is no '1 Day' and no 'TODAY!' string -- between one and two days out the plugin writes 'Tomorrow', and a passed countdown reads 'Nd ago' and is hidden unless show_expired is on.

Let a countdown save when its layout and style sections were never opened. The array-table editor keeps them in a hidden input, which comes back null or empty, and both were declared as strict objects -- so the config save failed with HTTP 400. Same defect reported against soccer-scoreboard as being unable to add a custom league; it belongs to the editor rather than to either plugin.

Fix config save failing with a 400 'Expected type string, got NoneType' when a countdown has no image. image_path is optional, so the schema now allows null (type: [string, null]) alongside a path string; the manager already coerces null to an empty string at runtime.

Config schema reorganized for a clearer setup experience: fine-tuning fields moved behind the web UI's collapsed Advanced Settings section (x-advanced). UX-only; no fields, defaults, or behavior changed.

Fix a blank-screen bug: _resolve_font() returned None (silently skipping all text) whenever the core's font_manager was unavailable or a lookup failed, with no fallback. It now falls back to PIL's default font, so a countdown's name/value are always visible even if the configured font can't be resolved.

Rewrite the README config section as a per-key table covering the v3 keys (target_time, mode, layout_preset, text_align, and the per-countdown style/layout overrides), add a title to the top-level enabled option, normalize the versions changelog key to ledmatrix_min_version, and set the manifest license to GPL-3.0 (project standard; the LICENSE file was already GPL).
